goal(c21-stage4): close the soundness gap - stage-4 fold drops the item byte reveal (Option A)

Owner decision 2026-08-01 (Decisions entry, c4f7fd52), executing option 1 of
docs/exec-plans/evidence/c21-stage4-analysis.md.

script_sources_stage_four consumed a TransactionFieldItemWitness carrying
the complete output bytes, so its one-step evidence grew with output size:
unbuildable above a 14,774-byte single-output best case against the
16,384-byte envelope, and practically bounded near 8,769 bytes by the
deployed direct-only carriage of semantic resolver 0. One-step resolution
is challenger-only and a ReadyForOneStep timeout awards nobody, so a
dishonest operator could finalize an invalid block by forging exactly that
fold step for a legal large output (CONFIRMED soundness gap, ledger row
2026-07-31).

The fold's successor consumes only the authenticated
(field_index, item_index, item_length, item_commitment) tuple:
bounded_collection_v1.verify_item binds that tuple (plus version) into the
outputs_hash from verify_native_tx_proof_source_v1 and stage 4 pins
field_index/item_index/item_count, leaving exactly one admissible tuple.
The byte reveal only re-proved that an authenticated commitment has a
preimage - which canonicalDecode (chunk + complete carriage) and the
stage-5 LedgerOutputProof traversal already establish for every output.

Stage 4 now expects the existing proof-only tag-29
TransactionRedeemerItemBeginWitness: no ABI change, no new constructor, no
bounded fallback, no 3.2 necessity artifact (carriage removed, not added).
Stage-4 evidence is O(1) in output size.

Evidence:
- Aiken focused batch 5/5: honest fold accepts; forged item_commitment
  rejects; forged item_length rejects with the successor held honest,
  isolating verify_item as the sole failing conjunct; stage 4->5 finish
  unchanged; canonical_decode control unaffected. The superseded
  mismatched-bytes test is replaced by two strictly stronger forged-tuple
  rejections.
- TS complete-item-proof-fit 4/4: the previously unprovable 16,384-byte
  maximum output builds a stage-4 argument (evidence < 2,048 bytes,
  auxiliary size equal across 256/14,774/16,384-byte outputs within CBOR
  integer width); carriage-policy + equivalence suites pass with the
  emitter inventory updated; package tsc exit 0.
- ledger-output-incremental-proof-v1.md residual-gap paragraph corrected
  (it understated the gap on both axes); validator-hash change invalidates
  all seven necessity artifacts - IG1 regeneration and re-measurement
  cascade tracked in the ledger.

goal(aiken): make the committed tree compile standalone - withdraw five protected-overlay dependents

redeemer-item-proof-v1.ak: the four dormant stage-one executor validators
and script-sources-redeemer-normalization-v1.test.ak reference
prevalidated_*/stage_data_*/FinalizeFrameTransitionV1 symbols that only the
protected overlay exports. Every local gate ran with the overlay present,
so this was invisible locally; Aiken CI failed at the fmt step before
reaching aiken check, masking it there too. CI (clean checkout) would fail
both 'aiken check' and midgard-node-ci's 'aiken build --env testnet'.

Resolution: index-only removal of the five files (working bytes untouched
and still hash-verified by the closure manifest) returning them to their
pre-636bb55f untracked protected-overlay status; they re-track in the same
commit that lands the source task's stage-one checkpoint. Constructor-aware
export scan shows no other committed file references overlay-only symbols.

Evidence: isolated clean-worktree 'aiken check --skip-tests' now passes
with 0 errors (pinned aiken v1.1.22+39d6b04 under a pseudo-TTY; a detached
run reproduces the known silent-exit pathology and is not evidence).
Closure manifest rebound for the five fmt-drifted protected-path hashes;
verifier reports current-tree-valid.

goal(vm): fix VM-DEFECT-7 - replay successor carries the grown source count

script_sources_replay_item built its successor with next_sources.count
(grown by replay_source_frontier when a resolved reference input carries a
script reference) but passed control.source_total_count unchanged, so
encode_script_sources_witness tripped its own
'expect source_total_count >= source_count' and the validator crashed on
every reachable replay step involving a reference script — the ordinary
reference-script pattern. No claimed_successor could make the step verify:
a completeness/liveness break of the dispute game, fixture-independent and
unfixable from the test side (full analysis: GOAL_PROGRESS.md 2026-07-31
VM-DEFECT-7 row; found by the disposition lane, seventh production defect
of this program).

The one-line fix passes next_sources.count at :8847, matching the
canonical TS reference model which advances both counters together
(validation-machine.ts:2090). Stage-7-12 equality demands are now
satisfiable after reference-script replay.

Evidence (pinned aiken v1.1.22+39d6b04, focused selectors):
- script_sources_replay_appends_reference_scripts — the standing failing

goal(analysis): C21-STAGE4-GAP confirmed as SOUNDNESS and wider than recorded

The row described (14,774, 16,384]. The practical gap is ~(8,769, 16,384].

14,774 derives from the witness encoding against the envelope, not the fold:
the producer rejects at evidenceCbor.length >= 16,384, and PlutusData chunks
bytestrings >64 bytes, giving E(N) = 2 + 66*floor(N/64) + pad(N mod 64).
E(14,774)=15,238 and E(14,775)=15,239 - a step of exactly 1, which pins the
fold's constant overhead uniquely at C=1,145.

But the binding bound is deployed carriage, not the producer guard. Stage 4
maps to semantic resolver 0 (validation-machine-data.ts:1014), which takes
its auxiliary INLINE, while submit.ts gates the reference route on
semanticResolverIndex === 1 at :3198/:3639/:4036. So a stage-4 complete item
must be inlined in both the prepare and semantic transactions, against a
measured direct frontier of 8,769. The pinned fixture is also a one-output
transaction, so the real frontier falls further as outputs grow.

Class is SOUNDNESS, not liveness: one-step resolution is challenger-only and
both timeout paths require ChallengerWins, so an operator can include a ~12KB
output, forge the stage-4 fold, and the honest challenger cannot produce the
evidence to win. The invalid block finalizes. An honest operator is never
harmed. Reachable - the ledger admits outputs to exactly 16,384 and the
capability floor mandates it.

Also found: verify_script_sources_stage_four_semantics_v1 is referenced by no
validator, only by tests - tested dead code.

Pre-existing protocol gap, not a regression from this Goal. Owner decision.
The lane ran nothing; every measured cell is marked MEASURE.

goal(node): NODE-ADMISSION-CLAIM is a TEST defect; production left untouched

The test asserted expect(claimedL2Transfers).toHaveLength(1) on the first
attempt. The only production caller treats that exact state as an ordinary
tick: tx-queue-processor.ts:553 returns processed:false, claimedCount:0 when
claimedLeases.length === 0 and re-claims next tick. The test was therefore
asserting strictly more than the contract the node itself relies on.

Forensics on the retained failing database: tx_admissions n_tup_ins=9,
n_tup_upd=0, xact_rollback=0 - the admit committed, nothing else touched the
row, the claim UPDATE matched zero rows. The passing run shows identical
n_tup_ins=9 with n_tup_upd=2. Transient, not structural. Claim machinery
independently sound at HEAD (tx-admissions-claim-load 9/9).

The fix is non-masking: the claim step polls within a bounded 30s, and if the
admission never becomes claimable it still hard-fails while dumping durable
row state, so a real liveness defect cannot hide behind the retry.

Also acting on the lane's second finding: this file is pervasively load-flaky.
Test 12 measured 236,718ms against a 240,000ms budget (1.4% headroom) and
241,974ms - already over - in another run. Raised to 900,000ms. The sibling
240,000ms budgets at :3353/3357/3361/3466/3564 remain unaudited, same class.

The mechanism is NOT proven: the instrumented probe never fired, so the cause
is eliminated-by-exclusion rather than observed, and no all-green full-file
run was achieved.

goal(fault-proofs): removal-site tx sizes measured; my 'inert relaxation' claim REFUTED

I previously recorded that the maxTxSize: 65_536 relaxation was inert because
Lucid caches protocol parameters at construction. That was wrong. The emulator
is constructed WITH the relaxed parameters before its Lucid instances
(:4116-4118), so Lucid caches 65,536 and the relaxation IS load-bearing.
Proven two ways: clamping the emulator's params to 16,384 propagates into
lucid.config(), and an identical build under 16,384 throws 'Max transaction
size of 16384 exceeded. Found: 20725' where 65,536 succeeds at 20,932.

All six requireReferenceScripts:false sites measured: 37,254-37,583 bytes,
20,870-21,199 OVER the L1 limit, each inlining 35,634 bytes of Plutus V3
validator bodies. Zero are safe. The already-fixed site re-measured at 1,868
bytes / +14,516 margin, reproducing exactly.

Second defect: :325-328 rejects a diagnostic snapshot whose max_tx_size is
not 16,384, and :371 then overwrites it with 65,536 - the guard is defeated
by the next line.

The six sites are NOT fixed here: my own brief prohibited the file they live
in. The lane correctly refused to fall back to a src edit, which would have
broken all six tests rather than fixing them.

Seventh relaxation found in spend-input-witness.test.ts, measured inert
(7,518 bytes, +8,866 margin), pinned to the default anyway. 1/1 pass.

goal(spec): remove orchestration prescription from GOAL_SPEC (owner-directed)

The spec no longer prescribes how work is organized, scheduled, sized, or
delegated. Removed in full: 5.1 Concurrency (concurrent-subagent limit and
its deferral to a GOAL_PROGRESS execution policy, Ultra-delegation guidance,
mandated per-subagent briefing format, parent-role definition) and 5.3
Recommended initial delegation (the prescribed two-agent F01/F02 wave).

PRESERVED and reframed actor-neutrally, because these constrain repository
state rather than who does the work: the shared-surface list, now 5.1
Serialization-sensitive surfaces, since concurrent edits there yield
incoherent integrations rather than honest merge conflicts; explicit path
ownership before concurrent work (4.3); non-overlapping path sets for
concurrent family tasks (9.3); and the task completion template, renumbered
5.2 and otherwise untouched. Vocabulary moved from lease/subagent to owned
paths/assignment at F05, C20-*, C83 and the goal:tasks:ready helper.

No acceptance criterion, gate, invariant, or evidence requirement changed -
12/14/15 and the gate sections are byte-identical. 1,505 -> 1,470 lines;
spec SHA-256 30a12ec9... -> a939e478..., ledger baseline rebound.

goal(core): C21 premise REFUTED - constant is 8,273; lane correctly refused to widen it

The parent's briefed premise was wrong. maxReliableDirectCompleteItemBytes
is 8,273 at HEAD, not 13,998, and 13_282 exists in no source constant.
Because the selector is 'itemBytes <= constant', 8,273 < 13,282 means the
briefed mis-selection is unreachable - there is no defect.

Rebinding to 13,282 as the row directed would have WIDENED direct-carriage
acceptance from 8,273 to 13,282 on a by-reference measurement basis that
does not match the deployed route (which embeds the validator, observation
limiting, referenceInputCount == 0). That is the asymmetric fix inv. 9
forbids, so the lane stopped instead. Seventh stale premise of the program.

Real hazard mitigated: the measurement script's 13,998 output is consumed
by nothing, so adopting it would have INTRODUCED the briefed defect. Its
misleading 'direct-proof' label is corrected to name the by-reference
basis; no measurement logic touched and output is byte-identical.

New test pins the frontier in BOTH directions (8,273 direct / 8,274
reference), mutation-verified by setting the constant to 13,998 and
confirming failure. The false row text is retained and marked refuted.
